newsitem.title: INDIA: India can expect polls in May or June-United Front.
newsitem.headline: India can expect polls in May or June-United Front.

text.p: India can expect general elections in May or June under a caretaker government headed by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, an official of the ruling United Front coalition said on Thursday.

"It is reasonable to expect elections in May or June," the official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters. "We are not only confident, but it is eminently reasonable that the caretaker government will be headed by Deve Gowda."

Asked if he expected the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to bail out the government, as suggested by some BJP leaders, by abstaining in a confidence vote on Friday, the official said such a move would not prevent early elections.

"They will do it only to kill us later. Why should we wait for that moment?" he said. "But we are really waiting to see how the BJP and the Congress, which claims to be secular, join hands against our secular government."

The official ruled out the possibility that the government would resign before the vote of confidence, saying the government formally opposed that option. Another United Front official had earlier said the government could resign before the vote.
United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said the government would seek a way to push the 1997/98 (April-March) budget through parliament before calling elections or dissolving the lower house.
